Subject: Follow-up: Model fit, benchmarks & quantization tradeoffs

Hi Alex — great meeting today, thanks for walking through Acme Health's assisted documentation use case. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can align the pilot: 

Summary from the call:
- Goal: provide an LLM assistant that summarizes and extracts structured data from patient-facing documentation with minimal hallucinations and PHI-safe handling.
- Primary success metrics: factual accuracy/hallucination rate (manual eval + automatic checks), instruction-following accuracy, and latency (p50/p95).
- Throughput target: pilot target ~200-300 tokens/sec inference per GPU; long-term target to keep cost under $0.015/token-equivalent (TBD).
- Compliance: PHI handling is critical — you flagged encryption/KMS and audit logs as must-haves.

Immediate asks I took away:
1) You to provide a small review dataset and the prompt sets you want us to use (thanks for promising that during the call).
2) Redwood to propose 2-3 candidate models and recommended quantization profiles + a plan for a 2-week pilot comparing quality and throughput.
3) Schedule SE deep-dive to align on eval harness and acceptance criteria.

What I'll send today:
- Proposed pilot scope and timeline (two-week comparison: one open model and one Redwood-verified model, each with AWQ and GPTQ/FP8 variants).
- A starter prompt set and the benchmarking harness link so you can drop your data.
- One-pager on quantization tradeoffs we discussed.

Attachments: acme_mvp_prompt_set_v1.json (starter prompts), quantization_tradeoff_onepager.pdf, latency_benchmark_3_seed.csv (example outputs).

Proposed next steps:
- You: upload the small review dataset and confirm whether we can use de-identified samples for the pilot.
- Redwood SE (cc'd Nikhil): propose exact model variants and a config for AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 runs.
- I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Monday to confirm acceptance criteria and compliance checklist.

If that looks right, I’ll send the kickoff invite and the pilot scope doc.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — super helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Dataset + scope: we'll upload ~1,200 de-identified notes (mix of triage + after-visit summaries). Priya will prep and drop in the Drive link by EOD tomorrow. We can use de-id for pilot; we will validate PHI removal on our side but may ask Redwood for guidance on any remaining edge cases.

2) Acceptance criteria: our internal rubric will weight hallucination/factuality more than minor stylistic issues. If quantization reduces hallucination recall, that's a non-starter.

3) Throughput & budget: 200-300 tokens/sec per GPU is our pilot target. We're evaluating cost for a production rollout, but for pilot we have a $25k evaluation budget.

4) Quantization ask: we specifically want to see AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 (if FP8 is supported on the hardware you plan to run). We are particularly concerned about instruction-following regressions post-quantization. Can you provide a short summary of expected quality delta and calibration needs?

Also: can Redwood run the two-week pilot in our AWS account (we prefer private VPC deployment) or will it run on Redwood-hosted Dedicated? Please call out any compliance gaps for PHI.

Thanks — Alex

Hi Alex — Nikhil from SE here. Thanks for the useful context. A few technical notes and a recommended pilot plan: 

Model candidates (to compare):
- Redwood-Raven-13B (Redwood-verified): strong instruction-following baseline; generally robust to AWQ.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B: good throughput/latency; smaller but often comparable on instruction tasks.
- Llama-2-13B-chat (ref fine-tuned): baseline for comparison.

Quantization tradeoffs (high level):
- AWQ: Usually preserves instruction-following quality well at 4-bit; slower quantization time but best quality retention for instruction-tuned weights. Tends to be our first recommendation for production pilots where quality is the priority.
- GPTQ: Faster to produce, smaller disk/RAM footprint; can introduce degradation for instruction prompts unless we do a per-layer calibration. Good for aggressive cost targets.
- FP8 (hardware-dependent): Offers significant throughput gains on supported GPUs (A800/A100X-class optimizations). Quality impact varies; requires careful calibration and sometimes mixed-precision kernels. Best used when target hardware supports FP8 and you can accept some calibration work.

Evaluation harness:
- We'll run the provided prompt set + your review dataset through each model+quantization combo and measure: hallucination rate (manual + heuristic), instruction-following score (automated rubric), latency p50/p95, and per-token cost estimate.
- Example benchmark outputs: https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/acme-health (I'll upload soon)

Pilot proposal (2 weeks):
Week 1: Run Redwood-Raven-13B (FP16 baseline) vs AWQ-4bit and GPTQ-4bit; collect metrics.
Week 2: Run Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16 baseline) vs AWQ-4bit and FP8 if hardware allows.
Deliverables: per-variant CSV of outputs, a short quality regression report, and a recommendation for production variant.

Attachments: quantization_tradeoff_onepager.pdf (summary), latency_benchmark_3_seed.csv (sample).

Regarding deployment: we can run the pilot either in your AWS account (Private deployment) or on Redwood Dedicated. For PHI, Private deployment with your VPC + KMS is preferred — we'll provide an infrastructure checklist and minimal IAM roles.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute tech kickoff — I suggest Mon 4/14 10am PT.

—Nikhil

1) Pilot environment: we prefer to run in our AWS account (Private deployment). Can you send the infra checklist and any expected schedule for access provisioning? Also confirm whether Redwood SE will need elevated IAM roles or if we can use cross-account roles with least privilege.

2) FP8 caveat: our infra team uses A10G/A30. If FP8 requires A800/A100X-class, then FP8 might not be possible for this pilot — that’s OK, we mainly want AWQ vs GPTQ comparison.

3) Costs: for the 2-week pilot we expect a ballpark estimate per-variant (compute + Redwood assist fee). Can you provide ballpark $ per GPU-hour for each config (FP16, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4, FP8) so we can pre-approve internally?

Alex — thanks for the quick replies and for prepping the data. Confirming next steps and pilot scope so all parties have the same expectations: 

Pilot scope (2-week):
- Models: Redwood-Raven-13B (FP16 baseline) and Mistral-Instruct-7B (FP16 baseline).
- Quantization variants to run: AWQ-4bit and GPTQ-4bit for both models. We'll attempt FP8 only if your infra supports it — per Alex note, A10G/A30 likely won't, so FP8 will be "stretch" if we can get access to compatible hardware.
- Data: your de-identified 1,200 notes + our starter prompt set (attached).
- Metrics: hallucination/factuality (manual + heuristic), instruction-following score, latency p50/p95, and cost-per-token estimate. Success threshold: hallucination reduction relative to current baseline and instruction-following > 90% on automated rubric (to be finalized in kickoff).
- Environment: preferred = your AWS account (Private deployment) using cross-account roles + KMS. Redwood will provide a minimal infra checklist and a playbook for least-privilege roles.

Deliverables and timeline:
- Day 0 (kickoff 4/14): finalize rubric & infra checklist.
- End of Week 1: Redwood shares initial CSV outputs for Raven (FP16, AWQ-4, GPTQ-4) + a short quality note.
- End of Week 2: Full comparison including Mistral runs and recommendation.
- Final: one-slide recommendation + a regression report.

Costs (ballpark per your $25k evaluation budget): we'll provide $/GPU-hour estimates in the kickoff doc. Early estimate: FP16 baseline ~ $6- $9 / GPU-hour (varies by instance), AWQ ~ similar compute-hours but lower memory footprint (enables cheaper instance sizes), GPTQ may allow smaller instances but requires extra calibration time up-front. Exact numbers in kickoff.

Action items:
- Alex/Priya: upload de-id dataset to the shared Drive and confirm KMS key and least-privilege access pattern.
- Nikhil: attach infra checklist + quick cost spreadsheet to the kickoff follow-up.
- Marissa: schedule pilot kickoff — invite sent (pilot_scope_calendar.ics attached).

If that matches your understanding, I’ll mark this as the pilot scope and we’ll start tomorrow.

Best,
